text_en: US existing home sales rose in September for the first time in four months, but surging mortgage rates and high home prices are expected to continue weighing on housing market activity for the rest of the year. Data released Tuesday by the National Association of Realtors showed that after August's sales figure was revised down, September closed existing home sales rose 1.5%, with the seasonally adjusted annualized pace reaching 3.99 million units, above the 3.95 million expected by surveyed economists. "Despite the pickup in sales, August and September were still the two weakest months for existing home sales this year. Mortgage rates have risen further in recent weeks, meaning fewer buyers qualify for home loans," NAR Chief Economist Lawrence Yun said in a statement.
